**Hypothesis driving this project** Marketers do not see the value of our existing widget library (and to some extend our personalization module) because widgets cannot be easily customized to their needs, so we expect that solving this problem will increase the overall satisfaction of customers with our Personalization module and increase our ability to convince marketers users during sales speech.

However, marketers can not simply create new widgets (eg. popin or banner) or adapt our existing widgets to their needs because we do not provide the right user experience or the right tools for that, so we expect that solving this problem will increase the satisfaction among our existing customers and improve our sales performance (especially when we are against AB Tasty)

**What is the project type and our justification for doing this project?** - Requested capability among SMB customers with no access to a technical team. - Some customers churned by the past to AB Tasty because they offered a more adapted product to their needs.

## 🚀 Feature Summary

Progressive \(gradual\) rollouts lets teams break up big releases into smaller chunks and remove most of the risks associated with releases by shrinking them into smaller, easier\-to\-control stages\. Users will be able to define the features and changes you are going to release, define who they are going to be released to, when they are going to be released, and what the increments look like\. --- ## 💁‍♂️ Problem\/Context

**Description:** As a Product, Engineering or QA user, I have no way of tapering my release\. I have to rely on the results of my pre\-prod QA to be assured that my release will not break anything major and consequently affect all of my user base\. I am also unable to plan for any sudden loads on bandwidth, storage or infrastructure when my new release is made public\.

- **Existing workaround:** None\. Currently, users would have to create individual rollouts for each individual increment\.

- **Justification:** A major selling point for some of our competitors\. Progressive rollouts are an established good practice and meets our audience's needs\. ---

## 💡 Solution

- **Product package:** Full stack - **User roles**: PM, EM, QA, RM \- or anyone concerned with product\/version releases\. - **Product scope:** The option can be found in the right overlay when adding a new rule in the Rollout Planner\. All UI changes reside in the same overlay\. - **Product design:** Selecting this option will prompt the user to define a few parameters:

1. Choose Progressive rollout when adding a new rule ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/b019216e125aaf2aa9da9f80bc8f02128c11b7c2c3f91fb6ffdbddddbcb6b1c5/image.png)

Then, in the next screen, fill in your parameters for progressive rollout:

1. Choose audience\/segment for this rule \(or create a new one\) 1. Start date  1. Initial exposure \(e\.g: 0%\) 1. Increment \(e\.g: 20%\)  1. Interval between increments \(e\.g: 5 days\) 1. Final exposure cap \(e\.g: 80%\) → Upon this final entry, the user sees an indication of when and at what exposure percentage the rollout will stop\.   ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/27fcda0472191b50264f4291e43a0b11159bf9fe4e8a84fa925327d9b464a06b/image.png) --- ## 🎯 **Measuring Success**

- **Market\-Fit:** This feature brings us on par with LaunchDarkly and Flagship, the only two competitors offering this functionality\. - **Adoption:** Once released, active customers try out progressive delivery at least once\. --- ## 📄 Attached documents

- **Figma file**: [https:\/\/www\.figma\.com\/file\/b8VwBwFMilgBCTJUH7DRKe\/Hybrid\-Plan?node\-id=400%3A75886](https://www.figma.com/file/b8VwBwFMilgBCTJUH7DRKe/Hybrid-Plan?node-id=400%3A75886) - **Redmine ticket**:

This correction helps against the [multiple comparisons problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple_comparisons_problem) basically, as we increase the number of variation, we increase the number of test statistics being computed and doing so, we increase the probability of being wrong\. Saying otherwise, as we add more variation, it becomes increasingly likely that one variation appears as a reliable winner due to random sampling error alone\.

To shield our customer from taking wrong conclusion we should implement a correction to the displayed reliability in case of multi\-variate testing \(it could be extended to goals in a second time\)\.

A first very simple correction would be the Bonferroni one, where we simply multiply the p\-value by the number of variations\.

A preferred and more advanced one would be the Holm\-Bonferroni one\. It requires to first sort all the p\-values of the tests, and then to multiply the smallest by the number of variations, the second smallest by the number of variation minus one etc\.

## 📒 **Feature short description:** Describe what the feature does\. ``` The Contentful Integration allows Contentful users to run experiments on content directly from Contentful UI and use Kameleoon powerful analytics solution to analyse the performance of those experiments. ```

**What is Contentful ?** Contentful is a headless CMS, a composable content platform that meets the unique demands of digital content and all the teams that produce and work with it\. Built with an API\-first architecture, Contentful orchestrates content from multiple sources and publishes it to any digital channel\. It ensures content is discoverable and reusable, provides tailored interfaces, and incorporates governance through role\-based access management and workflows\.

**What is a Headless content management system \(CMS\) ?** A headless CMS comprises three parts: a backend, APIs, and an interface\. The backend stores content and organizes data\. [APIs](https://www.contentful.com/blog/2015/10/22/contentful-a-content-platform/) connect the database to presentation layers\. These presentation layers are independent from the CMS and thus malleable\. Headless CMSes are defined by this lack of presentation layer\. \(If you were looking for it, this is the head in headless CMS\.\) Going headless allows you to distribute content through multiple channels on all sorts of platforms at scale\.

## 😥 Problem **Problem statement:** What problem are we trying to solve with this feature? Or, what is the opportunity we are addressing?  ``` As a Contentful user, I would like to have Contentful as the single source of truth when creating content for the different projects I manage (website, mobile app, etc). When I want to create an experiment with a version B on a Contentful content, I cannot do it in Contenful, I have to use Kameleoon graphic editor which is not convenient. I'd prefer to run experiments on content using the Contentful UI and use Kameleoon to analyse the performance on my experiment. ```

**Workaround:** - **Existing workaround:** Yes - **Workaround description:** asking a developer to use Contentful API in a coded experiment in Kameleoon\. ## 💡 Solution **Key benefits**: What value does this feature bring to the user?  ``` → Bringing experimentation capabilities to Contentful for users in charge of managing the website content through Contentful CMS → Keep Contentful as the single source of truth for your content. → Run advanced no-code experiments on structured content (copy, components, layouts and pages) managed in Contentful → Reduce the amount of manual work needed and get the best of both world: managing variants of an experiment in Contentful, benefiting from Kameleoon powerful experimentation engine and analytics solution → Marketers don't have to be dependent on developers to lead experimentation → No flicker: benefiting from server side instant bucketing by serving variations with no latency ``` **Use Cases:** Share use cases where this feature would help our users\. ``` → Run any experiments based on content (copy, components, layouts and pages) defined in Contentful and benefit from the best of both worlds. ```

column5: Create components to easily reuse any element anywhere
column6:
**Use case :** It can be very useful to reuse a same element either in the same widget (in the same screen or on other screens) or even in other widgets. For example, if you create a multi screens widget, you might need to reuse a same button on each screen.

**Solution proposed:** - From any screen of the "Design Tab", you can select any element and "Create a component" (clicking on the 3 dots icon) - Then, in the "Add element" section (on click on + icon), a new section "Components" appears, with the list of all components already defined. Choose on component of the section to add it to the screen being editied. - Later, if you decide to edit this component to update its design, all the changes will be applied for each instance of the component (in other words, you update the component only once, and the changes apply wherever the component is used) - If you want to apply a change only for a specific instance, you will be able to "Detach instance" (to make it independant from the component)

This "Component" feature can save designers a lot of time when creating their screens.

When designing a widget composed of different screens, it can be very useful to be able to duplicate an element in the other screens.

**Proposed solution:** - In the design tab \> left sidebar \> on click on the 3 dots for the element of your choice, a new action named "Duplicate in" appears. - On click, we can choose on which screen we want to duplicate the element.

**Notes:** - if the widget is only composed of 1 screen, the action is named "Duplicate" (as we don't have any screen to choose). - this feature is a bit similar to the "Create component" feature. The main difference is that the "Duplicate in" feature is only related to the widget currently being edited, and that each copy of an element is independant (which means if you apply changes on the raw element, the changes won't be applied on the different copies of the element)

## 💁‍♂️ Problem\/Context **Description:** As a data analyst, I would like to measure the long\-term impact of Kameleoon experiments always based on the same segment of excluded visitor\. We currently already get this feature on our personalization module \(we call it "control group" and allow users to define a percentage of excluded visitors from the configuration section of each project\), but not for our A\/B testing one\.

- **Existing workaround:** Not for the while \- starting from Q4 22, yes - **Workaround description:** Starting from Q4 22, yes, via Kameleoon Segment

**Project justification:** - **Project type:** Requested capability - **Justification:** - Feature requested by some prospects\. On 8th of July 22, requested by MongoDB - Deal lost \(Pandora, US customer\)\. One of the reason was the lack of reporting capabilities including Holdout\)\.

## What needs to be done? 1. For customers who subscribed to all our packages, A/B + Fullstack (FME), from the new "Projects" page, on click on "Add project": - project type field appears. We need first to rename the different options displayed in the dropdown. - we need to add a new option, in third position, called "Site: All types of campaigns". The goal of this option is to allow our customers who do both client side and SDK campaigns to have a fully customized javascript snippet suited to their needs (which was not the case with previous option Site SDK) - then, if this new option is selected, their is a specific installation process. The detailed specification related to these three points is avalaible on Figma, here: Note that the installation process doesn't change for already existing options (that are just renamed) 2. For customers who only get our fullstack (FME) package, from the new "Projects" page, on click on "Add project": - project type field appears (no change here) - just two options need to appear in the dropdown: "Site: SDK and hybrid campaigns" and "Mobile app (SDK campaigns)". In other words, the 2 other options displayed in this same dropdown in case 1 need to be removed. The behaviour when clicking on these options remains unchanged. 3. For all packages, when creating experiments, adapt the "project list" to make it coherent with the type of campaign: - from the experiment dashboard, when clicking on "New experiment" CTA, we first need to choose a type of campaign: graphic editor, or JS/CSS, SDK or hybrid - then, on the next popin, user needs to choose a project - in this list, we should only display the projects that are compatible with the chosen campaign type. Please refer to this table where I have summarized the expected behaviour (go the the second tab, called "By experiment type") : 4. Once all the points mentioned above are done, we will need to do a Database update for all our existing customers who get all our packages: A/B and fullstack (FME). For them, we will need to consider that all of their projects type are configured on the new option "Site: All types of campaigns"

For the engine part, we have two options: - Option 1 : The rebuild is successful \(we have a success status\), then we send a message in the queue \( `queue-kameleoon-js-file-ms` \) containing the sitecode\. This is what we are currently doing : we send a message \( through `queue-kameleoon-js-file-ms` \) to notify the CDN to purge the cache\. This action is triggered when the rebuild is successful\. - Option 2 : The rebuild respond with an OK\/KO status, then the engine will create a new queue \(like `queue-kameleoon-rebuild-status` \) and send an object containing the sitecode and the status\. This is what we can do if we would like to send a status with the sitecode, so this queue will be triggered whether the rebuild is successful or not \(compare to the `queue-kameleoon-js-file-ms` queue that is triggered only when the rebuild is successful, this is why there's no status in it\)\.

**Overview:** The Forced SDK Decision feature empowers developers to test and debug various application flows by overriding standard variation assignment\. It will allow developers to force specific users into predetermined variations, helping with experiment setup and debugging processes without using the Kameleoon app\.

**Key Benefits:** - **Controlled Testing:** Precisely manage which variation users experience, ideal for troubleshooting and validating experiments\. - **Enhanced Debugging:** Simplify debugging by forcing decisions at the SDK level, allowing quick identification of potential issues\. - **Customizable Flow:** Modify or remove forced decisions as needed, ensuring flexibility during testing\.

**Use Cases:** - Validating experiment setup before full rollout\. - Debugging user flows in development or production environments\. - Isolating specific variations for testing with specific user groups\.

- **Targeted Feature Flags:** Include or exclude visitors already targeted by another feature flag - **Targeted Web Experiment:** Include or exclude visitors already targeted by a web experiment\. - **Exclusive Feature Flag:** Includes only the users who are not already included in any active feature flag, web experiment, or both\. - **App version:** Target users based on the version of their mobile app\.

## 🚀 Feature Summary **Activity Logs** will effectively maintain a track of all Kameleoon user activities pertaining to Feature Flags that happened within a customer's account\. Users' activity will be logged automatically for any **creation**, **toggling**, **deletion**, or **editing** actions performed inside a feature flag, as well as show the status of the rule that was changed\. --- ## 😥 Problem - As a PM or Tech lead, when I want to see what changes were made within a feature flag, there is currently no way\. - **Workaround:** None ## 💡 Solution Benefits 1. **Keep track of changes:** Logs help leave a historical trail of all changes made to a flag's configuration\. In high\-stakes environments, logs are critical to be able to trace your steps back for debugging, potential rollbacks or identifying incorrect targeting conditions\. 1. **Transparent workflow management:** When experimentation, feature flags or delivery management have several stakeholders involved, not having a clear way to uphold accountability for actions can lead to problems and uncomfortable situations\. Logging ensures each action performed on Kameleoon can be linked back to individual users and thus ensure sanctity of daily operations 1. **Monitoring & Compliance:** Given the substantial overlap of DevOps with feature flagging, logs help find needles in a haystack, and subsequently make the software delivery cycle more secure and compliant 1. **Tech\. Debt Management:** A major challenge of working with feature flagging is the tech debt that accumulates over time\. Logs also help weed out flags that have become obsolete or orphaned\. ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/65e172ac15722631480c4d95145f78af3286712c2398c13a0e166b526bd10904/image.png)

**✏️ Product design:** - **Product package:** Feature Management and Experiment - **Product scope:** Rollout Planner - **Target Persona**: PM, Developer - **Main updates:** An additional menu item under the **Reporting** section, with a similar activity log as the main platform \(\+ filters adapted to the reported changes\) ## 🎯 **Measuring Success** - **Goal 1:** Drive more value for larger teams interested in this feature - **Success metric:** Feature adoption --- ## 📄 Attached documents - [Figma designs](https://www.figma.com/file/XCeroJVNp3J9xOS5dP9eH3/FF-In-Process?node-id=269%3A6536) - Redmine ticket:

## 📒 **Feature short description:**

This feature will allow users of FME to turn off a feature automatically if predefined KPI thresholds are met\. The user will be able to choose the KPIs that will act as triggers for the rollback, as well as the values at which the feature should turn off\.

The user can also choose the minimum number of visitors evaluated or time elapsed before the rollback condition takes effect, as well as the option to notify themselves or others if a rollback occurs\.

## 😥 Problem

**Problem statement:** - As a PM, dev or analyst, when I want to proactively turn off a poorly performing feature with minimal monitoring, there’s no way to set and forget\. - Even Progressive delivery rules, despite their slow ramp\-up, still need to be monitored manually\. - Implementing automatic feature rollbacks can be complex and time\-consuming, requiring significant effort to set up and maintain - I don’t have control over critical mass of customers to have been exposed before my guardrail takes action \(to ensure the rollback is not a false positive\) - I have to configure alerts from the results page and can only do so for experiments at the moment \- and the entire process is very disjoint from the creation step\. **Workaround:** - **Existing workaround:** Partially - **Workaround description:** Only for Feature Experiments ➜ Using the results page of experiments to create manual alerts for specific KPIs\.

## 💡 Solution **Key benefits**: 1. **Saves time and effort:** Automatic feature rollbacks save developers time and effort by automatically rolling back features that are causing issues or bugs, rather than having to manually identify and revert them\. 1. **Reduces downtime:** By quickly detecting and rolling back problematic features, automatic feature rollbacks can help reduce system downtime and minimize the impact on end\-users\. 1. **Improves stability:** By automatically detecting and rolling back problematic features, the overall stability of the system can be improved, reducing the likelihood of future issues\. **✏️ Product design:** - **Product package:** Feature Management - **Product scope:** Inside rule configuration overlay - **Target Persona**: All - **Main updates:** - Additional step when creating or editing a rule\. - User selects parameters for triggering rollback and the minimum thresholds\.

column5: Bot Filtering for Full Stack Experimentation
column6:
Websites today are commonly visited by **bots** and **spiders** which skew event tracking and conversion data by posing as actual human visitors\.

Experiment results can lose their value if numbers get inflated due to bot visits, which is why Kameleoon provides an easy solution for Full Stack customers to filter out bots with known [user agents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_agent) that are listed on the actively maintained [**IAB\/ABC**](https://www.iab.com/guidelines/iab-abc-international-spiders-bots-list/) database\.

> *The IAB has enlisted The Alliance for Audited Media to perform evaluation and management services associated with maintaining and publishing the industry Spider and Robot list, the use of which is required for compliance to the IAB’s Client Side Counting \(CSC\) Measurement Guidelines for “double pass” filtering\.* When tracking events with an SDK, Full Stack customers will need to simply pass their visitors' *user agent* attribute along with the other information for the bot to automatically be filtered\.

## 📒 **Feature summary:** An Edge CDN is cloud technology that specializes in static site hosting and serverless functions\. It provides developers with a seamless way to deploy and scale their websites, web applications, and APIs\. They focus on simplifying the deployment process and optimising the performance of web projects \- ensuring fast loading times and efficient delivery to end users\.

--- ## 💡 Solution benefits What value does this feature bring to the user? 

- **Improved website performance:** Edge CDN technologies distribute content closer to end users, reducing latency and improving website loading speeds\. This results in a better user experience and higher engagement levels\. - **Reduced bandwidth costs:** By caching content at edge server locations, edge CDNs help offload traffic from origin servers, reducing the bandwidth consumption and associated costs\. - **Enhanced scalability:** Edge CDNs offer scalable infrastructure that can handle high volumes of traffic without impacting performance\. This enables websites to accommodate sudden spikes in user activity or handle increased demand during peak periods\. - **Increased global reach:** With edge server locations distributed across the globe, edge CDNs can deliver content to users regardless of their geographical location\. This improves website accessibility and ensures consistent performance for users worldwide\. - **Improved reliability and resilience:** Edge CDNs use a distributed network of servers, reducing the risk of single points of failure\. If one edge server goes down, requests can be automatically rerouted to the nearest available server, ensuring continuous content delivery\. - **Flexibility and agility:** Edge CDNs provide flexibility in managing and delivering content\. They support dynamic content updates, enable A\/B testing, FF usage, and facilitate quick deployment of changes, allowing product teams to respond rapidly to user demands and market trends\.

## 🚀 Feature Summary

The goal of this feature is to introduce a **Multi\-Armed Bandit** for traffic allocation in Feature Experiment's variation split\. The MAB will optimize the distribution of user traffic among different feature variations, allowing for efficient and automated decision\-making during A\/B testing and experimentation\. --- ## 😥 Problem

- As a user, I face: - **Inefficient Traffic Allocation:** Challenges in determining the optimal allocation of user traffic among multiple feature variations during A\/B testing\. Manual allocation methods may result in suboptimal decisions and wasted opportunities\. - **Missed Opportunities:** Manual allocation, especially over several ongoing experiments may fail to leverage real\-time feedback from ongoing experiments, leading to missed opportunities to quickly identify and promote high\-performing variations\. - **Resource Drain:** Manual management of traffic allocation requires significant time and effort from me and my team, diverting their focus away from core tasks and slowing down the experimentation process\.

## 📒 **Feature short description:** Describe what the feature does\. ``` This feature is an enhancement to our graphic editor, specifically designed to streamline the creation of experiments. With this update, you now have the ability to effortlessly select elements on Single Page Applications (SPAs) where HTML IDs are not available or when they are not reliable due to dynamic behavior. ``` ## 😥 Problem **Problem statement:** What problem are we trying to solve with this feature? Or, what is the opportunity we are addressing?  ``` Previously, our graphic editor encountered difficulties in uniquely selecting elements on SPAs that lacked HTML IDs, making it challenging for users to apply layout changes effectively. ``` **Workaround:** - **Existing workaround:** No ## 💡 Solution **Key benefits**: What value does this feature bring to the user?  ``` We have implemented a solution that empowers you to specify how to select an element on the page, even in the absence of HTML IDs. Now, you can leverage custom attributes, such as "data-id," to uniquely identify elements and seamlessly incorporate them into your experiments. Key Features and Benefits: - Flexibility: Customers can indicate how to select elements on SPAs without relying on HTML IDs. - Custom Attribute Support: Utilize attributes like data-id to uniquely identify elements, enabling accurate selection for layout changes. - Streamlined Experiment Creation: With enhanced element selection, you can now effortlessly apply modifications within the graphic editor, simplifying the process of creating experiments on SPAs. ``` **✏️ Product design:** - **Product package:** Web Experimentation - **Product scope:** Project configuration page - **Target Persona**: Marketer - **Main updates:** In bullets, concisely describe what your solution consists of: - Navigate to the project configuration page\. - Access the new element selection option, which has been added alongside our existing option "Enable support for dynamic websites\." - Specify the desired method for selecting an element, such as using custom attributes like "data\-id\." ## 🎯 **Measuring Success** - **Goal 1:** usage of the feature - **Success metric:** nb of times the feature is activated in the project's configuration pages --- ## 📄 Attached documents - **Figma file**:

column5: Exclusive Widgets template for the National (Meta)
column6:
## Short Description: Some "Widgets templates" will be exclusively available at the national level\. Subsites can effortlessly inherit these widgets for national\-level campaigns, but when they create their own campaigns on their subsites, these templates won't appear, ensuring they're reserved for national campaigns only\. ## How will it works in practice? **For National:** - Addition of an "Exclusive National template" option \(in the widget template interface\) - Ability to select all widgets templates \(no change with current situation\)

**For subsites:** - Subsites will inherit widgets template coming from the Nation \(when used in duplicated campaigns\) - But such widget templates will be completely invisible for subsites, which means that: - "Exclusive National widget templates" won't appear in the Widget Dashboard - Subsites won't be able to create a new campaign using an "Exclusive national widget template" - Duplication of a campaign using an "exclusive nation widget template" will be impossible\.

The mechanism for duplicating a national campaign to the subsites can take some time\. It was not clear when the process was completed and whether any errors occurred during the duplication process\. The goal of this feature is to enhance this mechanism\. Now, a real\-time progress bar shows the duplication progress, and when an error occurs, the user is immediately notified \(along with the names of the subsites where the error occurred\)\.

BPCE receives every day and every week a report of all created personalizations\. In the export, you will now find a new column named 'Meta Personalization ID' for each personalization\. This column will display the ID of the meta personalization originating from the national level, which triggered the automatic duplication on subsites\. This addition provides better visibility and tracking of your personalizations across different levels of your campaigns\.

## 📒 **Feature short description:** Describe what the feature does\. ``` This feature allows Developers to easily incorporate and manage experiment-specific global code directly within the experiment. By providing a dedicated global code field, it enables the simulation of global scripts and facilitates the inclusion of temporary code for targeting purposes. The added benefit of automatic code removal upon experiment stopping ensures a clean and efficient process, contributing to overall performance optimization. ``` ## 😥 Problem **Problem statement:** What problem are we trying to solve with this feature? Or, what is the opportunity we are addressing?  ``` As a developer, when I want to implement experiment-specific global scripts or include temporary code for precise targeting in experiments, I encounter the following problems: Lack of a dedicated space within each experiment for global code management that only serves that experiment. The only way is to add that code to the global tracking script which has several drawbacks : - no possibility to simulate that code, - cluttered and less organized setup as the global script contains both temporary experiment code and tracking code for goals conversions..), resulting in potential performance issues and a lack of code cleanliness. ``` **Workaround:** - **Existing workaround:** Yes - **Workaround description:** adding that code to the Global Tracking Script ## 💡 Solution **Key benefits**: What value does this feature bring to the user?  ``` This feature streamlines the development process by providing a dedicated space for experiment-specific global code. Developers can now confidently implement and test code within the scope of each experiment, minimizing the risk of introducing bugs into the production environment. The separation of experiment code from the global tracking script eliminates the need for risky workarounds, contributing to a smoother and more reliable development experience. ``` **Use Cases:** Share use cases where this feature would help our users\. ``` When the developer wants to add temporary code (e.g., for targeting purposes), they want to seamlessly integrate and execute that code within the experiment setup, ensuring it is processed by Kameleoon before any targeting takes place. This enables developers to efficiently include temporary code for targeting purposes directly within the experiment, ensuring it gets executed by Kameleoon at the appropriate stage. This streamlines the development process and ensures precise targeting without compromising on the organization and execution of the code. ``` **✏️ Product design:** - **Product package:** Web Experimentation - **Product scope:** Code Editor - **Target Persona**: Developers ## 🎯 **Measuring Success**

column6: By default, Kameleoon downloads active experiments and includes them in the application file \(kameleoon\.js\)\. The browser stores and caches this file for 90 minutes\. If a user stops or modifies an experiment, targeted visitors returning to a page with active experiments within the 90\-minute caching period may still see the experiment due to the existing experiment configuration in the cached kameleoon\.js file\. To make more frequent updates without being impacted by browser caching, the Live\-Update Experiments feature refreshes any experiment tagged with “LIVE\-UPDATE” within one minute\. This is particularly useful for campaigns that require regular updates without being affected by browser caching\.

column6: # Implementation Notes \(Microsoft 2013\) - In general, the optimal pre\-experiment window is 1–2 weeks\. A shorter window doesn’t capture enough variance and a longer window captures noise\. - For longer experiments, a longer pre\-experiment window is needed to ensure that the same users are observed both during and prior to the experiment\. - CUPED performance is highly dependent on the metric; a metric with high variance across the user population will perform well\. - Make sure you that your covariate *X* will be evenly distributed between treatment and control\. If it’s systematically impacted by a treatment, CUPED becomes invalid\. - The CUPED method above only removes variance that can be accounted for linearly\. Non\-linear methods will be discussed in future posts\.

column6: ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/fe617ce10e2ad680f56fd2f5cb02e8d3e3c260a3005d59302a6cd18b42afb06b/image.png) ### **Problem Statement** Currently, there is no way to **configure or constrain AI\-generated content** across different features in the product \(AI Experiments, Graphical Editor, Widget Studio\)\. This lack of control forces users to manually adjust content every time they generate text, leading to inconsistencies in tone, compliance issues, and inefficiencies\. ### **Feature Principle** ✨ **Global AI Content Generation Customizations** introduce a centralized system for defining **rules and constraints** for AI\-generated content across all AI\-powered features in **AI Copilot**\. This allows users to **predefine guidelines** that shape AI outputs according to their brand, compliance requirements, and business needs\. ### **Key Functionalities** ✅ **Tone of Voice Configuration** – Users can select or create predefined tones of voice that the AI must follow across all content\.   ✅ **Restricted Keywords & Compliance Rules** – Users can specify words or phrases that AI should avoid to ensure brand safety and regulatory compliance\.   ✅ **Prompt Templates & Structure Constraints** – Users can enforce predefined content structures to maintain consistency across different AI use cases\.   ✅ **Protected Content Parameters** – Users can define elements that AI should not modify \(e\.g\., product names, legal disclaimers\)\.   ✅ **CSS & Content Exclusion Rules** – Allows users to exclude specific UI elements or text sections from AI processing\.   ✅ **Pre\-Treatment & Post\-Treatment Scripts** – Supports customization with JavaScript to preprocess or refine AI\-generated content before display\. ### **Expected Impact** 🚀 **More Control Over AI Outputs** – Ensures AI\-generated content aligns with business, legal, and branding guidelines\.   📈 **Efficiency Gains** – Reduces the need for repetitive manual edits by enforcing global content rules\.   ⚡ **Scalability & Consistency** – Provides a standardized AI configuration across AI Experiments, Graphical Editor, and Widget Studio, ensuring uniform output across the product\.

A synthetic control in the context of A\/B testing on the web is a method of analysis that is used to create an artificial control group when a real control group cannot be obtained due to limitations in the experiment\. Typically, a synthetic control is used when it is difficult or impossible to conduct a full randomized experiment with a real control group\.

This typically uses a statistical method that combines data from other groups, segments, or time to “simulate” the behavior that the control group might have if it existed\.

💡 <u>**Objective:**</u> Help users craft effective prompts by providing real\-time analysis and improvement suggestions\. ### <u>**Key Features:**</u> ✅ **Automatic Analysis:** Detects essential elements of a good prompt \(role, objective, context, format, etc\.\)\.   ✅ **Real\-Time Feedback:** Highlights strengths and weaknesses using ✅ \(validated\) or ❌ \(missing\/problematic\)\.   ✅ **Improvement Suggestions:** Provides precise recommendations to optimize the prompt \(e\.g\., "Add more context," "Clarify the objective"\)\.   ✅ **Templates & Examples:** Offers ready\-made prompts tailored to the user's needs\. ### <u>**Expected Impact :**</u> 🚀 **Prompting Made Accessible:** No need to be an expert to use an LLM effectively\.   ⚡ **Increased Efficiency:** Fewer iterations needed to get a relevant response\.   📈 **Enhanced Interaction Quality:** More precise answers that better fit user needs\.

### **Problem Statement** Currently, textual improvement suggestions are generated on a per\-page basis for product pages, which can lead to redundant efforts when multiple pages contain similar or identical content needing revision\. This approach can be inefficient and lacks a quantitative dimension to help prioritize which changes are most impactful\. ### **Feature Principle** When identical or very similar text improvements are detected across multiple pages \(for instance, dozens of pages sharing the same snippet\), the system should offer a single consolidated solution for all those pages, with two possible approaches: 1. **LLM\-Driven \(Automatic\)**:      The LLM automatically selects the best improvement proposal based on context and text quality across those pages\. 1. **User\-Driven \(Tabular View\)**:      A table displays different potential improvements, allowing the user to choose the most appropriate one based on quantitative criteria such as:     - **Readability Score** \(e\.g\., Flesch\-Kincaid\)     - **SEO Impact Estimation** \(e\.g\., presence of relevant keywords\)     - **Estimated Conversion Rate** \(if available, based on historical data or industry benchmarks\)     - **Contextual Relevance** \(a rating of how well the text aligns with the page’s intent and best writing practices\) #### **Quantitative Data to Include** - **Frequency of Occurrence**: The number of pages containing the text snippet to justify a single consolidated proposal\. - **Comparative Analysis**: Evaluation of different proposals regarding readability, SEO potential, and historical performance\. - **User Engagement Impact**: Potential effect of the changes on metrics like time on page or bounce rate\. ### **Expected Impact** - **Reduced Redundancy**: Centralized management of similar text improvements across multiple pages, ensuring a more consistent user experience\. - **Increased Relevance**: Quantitative data helps users make more informed decisions about which improvements to apply\. - **Productivity Gains**: Users can swiftly apply the best suggestions to multiple pages without addressing each page individually\.

A **custom bucketing key** will allow you to control how users are consistently assigned to variations based on a user\-defined identifier rather than the default one \(visitor code\)\. This is especially useful when your customers such as agencies \(or certain applications\) need to group users differently than the default logic — for example, by account ID, session ID, device ID, or any other relevant key in your business logic\. By using a custom bucketing key, you ensure that the same entity \(e\.g\., a company or group\) always gets the same variation, even if individual users change or switch devices\. It’s also helpful in B2B contexts where features should be rolled out at the **account level**, not the user level\. This flexibility gives you greater targeting precision, consistency, and control in your rollouts and experiments\.
